subject: Next steps: inference environment preference & migration map
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Roberta Singh <roberta@acornhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Cho <ben.cho@acornhealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-29T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: quick recap & suggested runway

Hi Roberta / Ben —

Great to connect earlier. Quick recap from our side and a suggested 2-week "runway" to make a deployment decision:

- Summary of fit: Acorn’s primary goal is sub-75ms 1kB token latency for real-time triage and predictable cost for throughput spikes. You run nightly batch jobs on a legacy GPU cluster and also have some inference calls to a 3rd-party API for customer-facing features.
- Deployment asks we heard: data residency (US-only), predictable throughput for daytime surge, and minimal engineering lift for an initial cutover.

Initial recommendation (based on the call):
1) Proof-of-concept: Redwood Hosted API to validate latency and integration surface quickly (2–3 days).
2) Mid-term: Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) if you need predictability and isolation; keeps origin traffic routing simple.
3) Long-term: Private VPC only if you require on-prem or strict KMS/HSM separation.

Two quick asks so we can size options and produce a mutual action plan (MAP):
- Can you share the rough qps/TP50 token profile for peak windows and the nightly throughput (tokens/hour)?
- Are there procurement constraints that would push you immediately to a VPC/on-prem option?

I attached a short one-pager comparing Dedicated vs VPC and a starter MAP (editable). If helpful, Karthik can propose a migration path from your GPU cluster (lift-and-shift vs staged dual-run).

Next step: propose a 30-minute technical follow-up with your infra lead this week to validate the KV cache / batch limits. Are mornings PST best?

Thanks —
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Roberta Singh <roberta@acornhealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Cho <ben.cho@acornhealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: quick recap & suggested runway

Thanks, Tessa —

This is helpful. A few clarifications from our side:
- Our daytime peak is about 120 qps with median request sizes around 800–1,200 tokens; nightly batch jobs push ~40M tokens over 4–6 hours.
- Current infra: a cluster of mixed GPUs (V100 + A100 in an on-prem colo) that we use for heavy batch and occasional inference. We also have a small allocation to an external API for low-latency features.
- Procurement: we prefer to start with a hosted option to move fast; procurement will only commit to reserved Dedicated after a 60-day POC and SOW.

We can do a technical sync with our infra lead, Marcus (cc'd on my side), tomorrow 10:30am PST.

Two asks from us:
1) Can Redwood host a short runbook of the migration paths so Marcus can review? Specifically curious about (a) dual-run approach where we mirror a small percentage to Redwood while keeping nightly batch on-prem, and (b) an accelerated lift-and-shift for batch only.
2) Costing: a ballpark comparison for Hosted (pay-as-you-go) vs Dedicated reserved (monthly commit) for our peak/batch profile — ballpark numbers are fine for now.

Roberta
Director of Platform Engineering, Acorn Health
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Roberta Singh <roberta@acornhealth.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-31T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: quick recap & suggested runway

Roberta —

Thanks for the profile. A few technical notes that will help us size and recommend the migration flow:

- Latency/throughput: For 120 qps with 1k token median, Dedicated with 2 x A100-like nodes in a reserved pool gives predictable TP50/95 and predictable costing; Hosted can serve initial spikes but may require batching tuning to meet 75ms TP50 depending on request concurrency.
- Batch migration: If the nightly jobs are GPU-heavy but can be split into shards, we normally recommend porting batch jobs first to a Dedicated pool (lift-and-shift) or to Private VPC if you need the data plane co-located with storage.
- Dual-run approach: We can mirror 5–10% traffic to Redwood Hosted (or Dedicated) with prefix caching enabled; that gives immediate quality/regression checks while keeping primary traffic on-prem. We will need a small wrapper to replicate request signatures for traceability.
- KV cache and continuous batching: We will need to know sequence-length distribution and whether requests are chat-like (with long histories) vs stateless prompts.

I'll prepare a short runbook with the two migration options Roberta asked for and a sample cost sketch (hosted vs 6-month vs 12-month reserved commit). Marissa — I can include an ops checklist for procurement.

-Karthik
Lead Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-06-01T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: MAP & proposal: 2-week runway (POC) + options

Roberta / Ben —

Attached is the editable MAP (MAP-AcornHealth.xlsx) and the one-pager. High level proposal:
- Week 0–1: Stand up Hosted integration + smoke tests (validate latency/outputs on a replicate dataset).
- Week 2–4: Mirror 10% of daytime traffic to Redwood (Hosted or Dedicated trial) and run nightly batch sample on Dedicated nodes to validate batch cost and perf.
- Decision point (end of week 4): commit to Dedicated (6/12 month) or move to Private VPC for data residency.

Action items
- Acorn: provide sample token histogram (peak windows + nightly job manifest) and name of infra lead (Marcus confirmed on your thread).
- Redwood: Karthik to deliver migration runbook + ballpark costing table.

Can we lock the technical sync for tomorrow at 10:30am PST? I'll send a calendar invite.

Regards,
Tessa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
